description: SASRec predicts the next interaction using causal self-attention over a user's item history. Item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting features score candidate items through shared item embeddings. Training uses positive next items and sampled negatives. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
motivation: Attention can emphasize recent interactions in sparse histories while retaining access to older relevant actions. The supplied task establishes SASRec as the starting baseline; it does not specify a new cold-start mechanism. ID-based SASRec alone cannot learn useful representations for items absent from training.
implementation_notes: Retain RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and routing for all four categories. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the environment's SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Keep splits and host evaluation unchanged; select using macro validation HR@10. Store artifacts beneath the trial directory and keep predictor generation consistent with trained checkpoints. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and the supplied compatibility contract. Any proposed content extension must use only permitted public metadata and requires validation; no benchmark improvement is established here.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load unchanged RecHarness splits and item mapping.
  Initialize SASRec with seed 42.
  For each training batch:
    Embed padded item sequences and positions.
    Apply causal attention and feed-forward blocks.
    Score positive next items and sampled negatives.
    Minimize binary cross-entropy over valid positions.
  Save checkpoints and architecture configuration beneath the trial directory.
Generate working/predict.py with matching architecture and category routing.
Use the pinned host validation protocol to compare trials by macro HR@10.

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an influential attention-based approach to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: Relative to the required RecHarness baseline, the supplied idea adds no concrete architectural or training innovation. Scores use a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Permitted titles and descriptions could support a separately validated extension for sparse item histories.
future_potential.negative: Such an extension is unspecified, and its benefit under the fixed evaluation and search budget is unknown.

code_difficulty.positive: Starting from the existing SASRec implementation makes baseline integration relatively straightforward; higher scores indicate greater difficulty.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require synchronized checkpoint loading, predictor generation, dataset routing, and diagnostic adapters.
